title: Naming conventions and component classes
learningObjectives: Explain naming conventions and component classes and organise styles for maintainability.

understand.concept: CSS naming conventions give classes predictable meanings and boundaries. Component-oriented names can describe a component and its parts, while utility classes describe a single reusable purpose. BEM is one optional convention, not a browser requirement.
understand.whyItMatters: Consistent names reduce accidental selector overlap and help teams find styles. Avoid names tied only to temporary appearance or one page location when a component is reusable.
understand.analogy: Class names are labels on reusable tools: clear labels make it easier to find and maintain the right tool.
understand.analogyLimit: The analogy is simplified; CSS cascade, inheritance, and conditional rules follow the formal cascade and at-rule processing model.

explain.narrative: The component name and its element names describe the card and its internal parts without relying on a deeply nested selector.
